content: I've opened a PR which gives an implementation and correctness proof (via mvcgen) of randomized quicksort.
Currently the expected runtime analysis is left out, perhaps someone with a good grasp of Mathlib's probability theory library can help with this

mvcgen follows from a WP instance I've provided for our random sampling model. Currently it is such that a postcondition holds when it holds for all possible outcomes in the distribution. This allows us to use mvcgen prove things like random quick sort where the outcome is certain (it will always sort a list).

However randomized algorithms where outcomes are probabilistic require some kind of probabilistic program logic. Which even if formalized, would not be connected to the current WP infrastructure provided by Lean core.

@Sebastian Graf I recall that you were working on generalizing mvcgen, would supporting a probabilistic program logic be within scope of this?

Yes! The new tactic is called vcgen and its WP class can connect to any CompleteLattice as a program logic that you like! In particular, some subtype of σ -> ENNReal should be possible.

I'm working hard towards a release of vcgen; it is mostly lacking documentation at this point.
what would a suitable probabilistic program logic for algorithmic reasoning look like? Perhaps you know @Markus de Medeiros and @Bas Spitters ?

I have the Dijkstra monad one in CatCrypt, ported from SSProve. I have a tactic related to vcgen which I hope to release in a week or two.
https://github.com/spitters/catCrypt-core/

I don't know about what it would look like in vcgen, but we verified the ERT of quicksort in Tachis. I already ported its sister logic Eris to Iris-Lean, so that's one version of what this could look like.

I'd love to see what this looks like in vcgen and plan to explore more about Eris+vcgen soon :)

I don’t think quicksort illustrates a probabilistic algorithm in the sense of correctness guarantees themselves being probabilistic (think bloom filter or kargers min cut algorithm). I was able to coax gpt 6 into producing the expected running time here https://github.com/Shreyas4991/Algolean/pull/87
